# Purpose

This file implements **Ana revision-plan Step 18: race and ethnicity denominators**.

The existing race analysis in File 04 is intentionally case-based only: it reports the
distribution of confirmed chikungunya cases/deaths and race-specific case fatality, but it does
**not** use a population denominator.

Here we add a denominator-matched analysis using the **IBGE 2022 Census population by
self-declared color/race at macro-region level**.

Primary analysis:
- Numerator: confirmed chikungunya cases notified in **calendar year 2022**
- Denominator: **2022 Census resident population** in the matching macro-region and
  color/race category
- Outcome: confirmed chikungunya incidence per 100,000 population

Secondary descriptive analysis:
- 2016-2025 confirmed cases divided by the 2022 Census race-specific population.
- This is labeled **cumulative reported case burden per 100,000 2022 Census population**,
  not annual incidence, because a single 2022 denominator is not an annual population series.

Important:
- Missing/unknown SINAN race is not assigned to any racial/ethnic group.
- The denominator uses the IBGE **cor ou raça** Indigenous count, not the broader total
  Indigenous population that also includes persons identified through the separate
  "se considera indígena" question. This matches SINAN's race/color field more closely.
- This analysis is descriptive and does not establish causal racial/ethnic disparities.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = TRUE, message = TRUE)

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(scales)
  library(readr)
})

STUDY_START_YEAR <- 2016L
STUDY_END_YEAR <- 2025L
DENOM_YEAR <- 2022L

RESULT_ROOT <- path.expand("~/Downloads/inla_results")
OUT_DIR <- file.path(RESULT_ROOT, "race_ethnicity_denominators_IBGE2022")
dir.create(OUT_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

if (!exists("Chik_total")) {
  stop(
    "Chik_total is not currently in memory. Run 01_data_import_cleaning.Rmd once in this ",
    "R session, then rerun File 21."
  )
}
```

# 1. IBGE 2022 Census denominators

Source:
IBGE, Censo Demográfico 2022, resident population by self-declared color/race and
Grandes Regiões. The Indigenous counts below are the **cor ou raça indígena**
counts, not the broader Indigenous-population total.

```{r ibge-denominators}
ibge_race_region_2022 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~region,        ~race_label,       ~population_2022,
  "North",        "White",                  3598298,
  "North",        "Black",                  1530418,
  "North",        "Asian",                    29467,
  "North",        "Pardo (Mixed)",         11654390,
  "North",        "Indigenous",              539821,

  "Northeast",    "White",                 14571557,
  "Northeast",    "Black",                  7127018,
  "Northeast",    "Asian",                    68749,
  "Northeast",    "Pardo (Mixed)",         32559846,
  "Northeast",    "Indigenous",              327725,

  "Southeast",    "White",                 42318768,
  "Southeast",    "Black",                  9003372,
  "Southeast",    "Asian",                   570852,
  "Southeast",    "Pardo (Mixed)",         32833389,
  "Southeast",    "Indigenous",              109934,

  "South",        "White",                 21729713,
  "South",        "Black",                  1505526,
  "South",        "Asian",                   120838,
  "South",        "Pardo (Mixed)",          6499382,
  "South",        "Indigenous",               81478,

  "Central-West", "White",                  6033785,
  "Central-West", "Black",                  1490124,
  "Central-West", "Asian",                    60224,
  "Central-West", "Pardo (Mixed)",          8536279,
  "Central-West", "Indigenous",              168684
)

national_check <- ibge_race_region_2022 %>%
  group_by(race_label) %>%
  summarise(population_2022 = sum(population_2022), .groups = "drop")

print(national_check)

expected_national <- tibble::tribble(
  ~race_label,       ~expected_population,
  "White",                  88252121,
  "Black",                  20656458,
  "Asian",                    850130,
  "Pardo (Mixed)",          92083286,
  "Indigenous",              1227642
)

denom_check <- national_check %>%
  left_join(expected_national, by = "race_label") %>%
  mutate(diff = population_2022 - expected_population)

print(denom_check)

stopifnot(all(denom_check$diff == 0L))
```

# 2. Prepare confirmed SINAN cases and map macro-region

```{r prepare-cases}
race_lut <- c(
  `1` = "White",
  `2` = "Black",
  `3` = "Asian",
  `4` = "Pardo (Mixed)",
  `5` = "Indigenous",
  `9` = "Unknown"
)

state_region_lookup <- tibble::tribble(
  ~uf_code, ~region,
  "11", "North",
  "12", "North",
  "13", "North",
  "14", "North",
  "15", "North",
  "16", "North",
  "17", "North",

  "21", "Northeast",
  "22", "Northeast",
  "23", "Northeast",
  "24", "Northeast",
  "25", "Northeast",
  "26", "Northeast",
  "27", "Northeast",
  "28", "Northeast",
  "29", "Northeast",

  "31", "Southeast",
  "32", "Southeast",
  "33", "Southeast",
  "35", "Southeast",

  "41", "South",
  "42", "South",
  "43", "South",

  "50", "Central-West",
  "51", "Central-West",
  "52", "Central-West",
  "53", "Central-West"
)

race_cases <- Chik_total %>%
  mutate(
    year = lubridate::year(as.Date(DT_SIN_PRI)),
    code_muni = stringr::str_pad(
      substr(as.character(ID_MUNICIP), 1, 6),
      width = 6,
      side = "left",
      pad = "0"
    ),
    uf_code = substr(code_muni, 1, 2),
    race_code = as.character(CS_RACA),
    race_label = dplyr::recode(
      race_code,
      !!!race_lut,
      .default = "Missing/other"
    ),
    race_named = race_code %in% as.character(1:5)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    CLASSI_FIN %in% c(1, 13),
    year >= STUDY_START_YEAR,
    year <= STUDY_END_YEAR
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    state_region_lookup,
    by = "uf_code"
  )

stopifnot(!anyNA(race_cases$region))

cat("Confirmed cases, 2016-2025:", nrow(race_cases), "\n")
```

# 3. Race missingness by macro-region

```{r missingness}
race_missingness_region <- race_cases %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(
    confirmed_cases = n(),
    named_race_cases = sum(race_named),
    missing_unknown_race = sum(!race_named),
    missing_unknown_percent =
      100 * missing_unknown_race / confirmed_cases,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(missing_unknown_percent))

print(race_missingness_region)
```

# 4. Primary analysis: 2022 race-specific incidence

This is the clean denominator-matched analysis because numerator and denominator refer to
the same calendar year.

```{r incidence-2022}
race_cases_2022 <- race_cases %>%
  filter(
    year == DENOM_YEAR,
    race_named
  ) %>%
  count(
    region,
    race_label,
    name = "cases_2022"
  )

race_incidence_2022 <- ibge_race_region_2022 %>%
  left_join(
    race_cases_2022,
    by = c("region", "race_label")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    cases_2022 = tidyr::replace_na(cases_2022, 0L),
    incidence_per_100k =
      1e5 * cases_2022 / population_2022
  ) %>%
  arrange(region, desc(incidence_per_100k))

print(race_incidence_2022, n = Inf)

stopifnot(
  nrow(race_incidence_2022) == 25L,
  all(race_incidence_2022$population_2022 > 0),
  all(is.finite(race_incidence_2022$incidence_per_100k))
)
```

# 5. National 2022 race-specific incidence

```{r national-2022}
national_race_2022 <- race_incidence_2022 %>%
  group_by(race_label) %>%
  summarise(
    cases_2022 = sum(cases_2022),
    population_2022 = sum(population_2022),
    incidence_per_100k =
      1e5 * cases_2022 / population_2022,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(incidence_per_100k))

print(national_race_2022)
```

# 6. Secondary: cumulative 2016-2025 burden relative to 2022 Census population

This is **not** called incidence. It is retained only to show the full study-period case
distribution relative to a common census denominator.

```{r cumulative-burden}
race_cases_full <- race_cases %>%
  filter(race_named) %>%
  count(
    region,
    race_label,
    name = "cases_2016_2025"
  )

race_cumulative_burden <- ibge_race_region_2022 %>%
  left_join(
    race_cases_full,
    by = c("region", "race_label")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    cases_2016_2025 =
      tidyr::replace_na(cases_2016_2025, 0L),
    cumulative_cases_per_100k_2022_population =
      1e5 * cases_2016_2025 / population_2022
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    region,
    desc(cumulative_cases_per_100k_2022_population)
  )

print(race_cumulative_burden, n = Inf)
```

# 7. 2022 macro-region figure

```{r figure, fig.width=8.2, fig.height=5.2}
p_race_incidence_2022 <- ggplot(
  race_incidence_2022,
  aes(
    x = race_label,
    y = incidence_per_100k,
    shape = race_label
  )
) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ region,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Race / ethnicity",
    y = "Confirmed chikungunya incidence per 100,000",
    title = "Race-specific confirmed chikungunya incidence by macro-region, Brazil, 2022"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 35,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )

print(p_race_incidence_2022)
```

# 8. Compare case composition with population composition in 2022

This is useful for interpretation but should not replace the incidence rates.

```{r composition}
population_composition_2022 <- ibge_race_region_2022 %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  mutate(
    population_share =
      population_2022 / sum(population_2022)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

case_composition_2022 <- race_cases %>%
  filter(
    year == DENOM_YEAR,
    race_named
  ) %>%
  count(
    region,
    race_label,
    name = "cases_2022"
  ) %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  mutate(
    case_share =
      cases_2022 / sum(cases_2022)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

composition_compare_2022 <- population_composition_2022 %>%
  select(
    region,
    race_label,
    population_2022,
    population_share
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    case_composition_2022,
    by = c("region", "race_label")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    cases_2022 = tidyr::replace_na(cases_2022, 0L),
    case_share = tidyr::replace_na(case_share, 0)
  )

print(composition_compare_2022, n = Inf)
```

# Interpretation guardrails

1. The **primary race-specific incidence result is 2022 only**, because that is the year for
   which the numerator and census denominator align exactly.
2. The 2016-2025 calculation uses the 2022 Census denominator only as a common reference;
   call it cumulative reported case burden, not annual incidence.
3. Missing/unknown SINAN race remains substantial and can vary geographically.
4. These rates describe confirmed/notified disease burden and therefore remain sensitive to
   access to care, case ascertainment, diagnostic capacity, and race recording completeness.
5. Do not describe differences as biological susceptibility or causal effects of race/ethnicity.
